hints.title: Polygon Triangulation Edge Partitioning
hints.text: Every triangulation of a polygon with vertices 0 through n - 1 must connect the boundary edge between vertex i and vertex j with some intermediate vertex k.

hints.title: Intermediate Triangle Division Principle
hints.text: Choosing intermediate vertex k with i < k < j creates triangle (i, k, j) and splits the polygon into independent sub-polygons [i, k] and [k, j].

hints.title: Interval Length Order DP Execution
hints.text: Construct an n by n table where dp[i][j] is the minimum score for triangulation from vertex i to vertex j. Base intervals of length two contribute zero cost. Increase the interval span from three to n, computing for each pair (i, j) the minimum of dp[i][k] plus dp[k][j] plus values[i]*values[k]*values[j] across all k. Return dp[0][n - 1].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input size or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N^3) time and O(N^2) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: There are Catalan number C(n-2) possible triangulations, causing combinatorial explosion.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Interval DP memoizes sub-polygon ranges in O(n^2) space and computes optimal scores in O(n^3) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize how a fixed boundary edge pins one triangle, splitting the polygon into two independent sub-problems.
